steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Finance cannot reconcile instance uptime. A metered machine in an account dedicated to one customer belongs to that customer regardless of which customer its tags name, including when they name none. A shared-account machine may belong to several customers and its uptime must be divided evenly among tenants genuinely onboarded for that account; unknown or unplaceable usage stays off the bill. The onboarding records in the metering bucket beside the account list identify billable customers. Update the metering sweep so published uptime follows those rules. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.
3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `local-usage-data` bucket, the `local-config` bucket and the `metering` org. **Case sensitive**.
5. [Get an API Token from the Influx instance](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/security/tokens/create-token/)
6. Create the following file at the root directory of the project named `.env`, where the `INFLUX_URL`, `INFLUX_TOKEN` and `INFLUX_ORG` values are stored

Your token will be different than the one below.

steps.message:
The implementation is complete. Summary of changes:

1. **`src/utils/aws/s3.ts`** — added `listDocumentKeys(Bucket, Prefix)` with pagination so collectors can enumerate the per-customer onboarding records sitting beside the account list.

2. **`src/onboarding/entities/meteringAccounts.entity.ts`** — added `CustomerOnboardingRecord` / `CustomerAccountOnboarding` / `AccountTenancy`, plus:
   - `MeteringRegistry.loadCustomerRecords()` — reads every onboarding record under `customerRecordPrefix` (these are the only billable customers), tolerating unreadable objects.
   - `MeteringRegistry.resolveTenancy()` — builds per-account tenant lists and marks an account dedicated when exactly one customer claims it (conflicting claims fall back to shared).

3. **`src/microservices/ec2InstanceDataGatherer/ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.ts`** — `gatherUsage` now resolves tenancy before attributing running time via new `resolveOwners`:
   - dedicated account → all of its metered instances bill to that customer, whatever the tags say (including untagged or tags naming someone else);
   - shared account → the increment is split evenly among the tagged customers genuinely onboarded for that account;
   - untagged/unknown/unplaceable instances (and accounts nobody is onboarded for) are skipped and logged, keeping them off the bill.

4. Added `ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.spec.ts` covering dedicated accounts, even splitting, unknown tenants, orphan accounts, conflicting dedication, whitespace/duplicate tags, and empty registries. Verified live against the emulator: `cus_harbor` = 3.5 × increment (4 instances incl. half of the shared one), `cus_lattice` = 1.5 × increment; the untagged shared instance is dropped. Full unit suite shows only pre-existing, unrelated network failures.
